deviations.what: PolicyError subclasses CliError and carries EXIT_POLICY_DENIED (3) instead of being a structural look-alike with exit code 1
deviations.reason: t3's brief told it to keep core free of CLI imports while t1 and t5 were told to import CliError, so wave 0 shipped two error contracts; main() catches CliError by name and wraps anything else as 'unexpected: file a bug', so a policy refusal would have surfaced as an internal defect. Exit code 1 also contradicted spec honesty condition h5, which requires policy denial to carry its own documented code — t3 used 1 only because its brief predated t7's taxonomy band. APPLIED DURING THE MERGE GATE before this record was written.

deviations.what: failure-category tag renders in emit_error instead of being prefixed onto CliError.message
deviations.reason: t7's acceptance criterion required the category to be distinguishable in TEXT error output, but its brief scoped headspace/cli/_output.py out of its file list, leaving message mutation as the only reachable workaround. That mutated a field callers read and duplicated the category already present in to_dict(). The fix edits _output.py, which no wave-0 task owned. t7's tests asserted the behaviour rather than the mechanism, so they pass unchanged. APPLIED DURING THE MERGE GATE before this record was written.

deviations.what: assign the ArtifactRecord to result.Artifact mapping explicitly to t10
deviations.reason: t2 and t6 independently defined artifact vocabularies that do not line up (t6: name, content_type, purpose, retention, size_bytes, sha256; t2: name, purpose, media_type, digest, size_bytes, reference). t6's to_list() is documented as feeding the result package's artifact section but cannot construct t2's Artifact directly. The plan gave t2 and t7 a shared status vocabulary but never gave t2 and t6 a shared artifact one, so no task owns the mapping. NOT YET APPLIED — this amends t10's brief before wave 2 starts.

deviations.what: workspaces hold at ready with an active_jobs count and never enter the running state; t10 adds a running->ready edge so the spec's running state becomes real
deviations.reason: t1 built TRANSITIONS as a strict DAG with no edge back to ready, so ready->running->completed would exhaust a workspace's lifecycle on its first job — yet spec FR-07 requires multiple jobs to share one session and doc section 6 stage 4 (Execute) describes exactly that. t8 resolved the conflict by never entering running, which leaves a state named in spec claim c2 unreachable in practice and forces t8's destroy-during-run refusal to synthesize its error by asking the table about a transition no workspace actually makes. Resolution assigned to t10: add running->ready to states.py and drive ready->running->ready around each job, which makes the state real and turns the synthesized guard into a genuine one.

deviations.what: the docker SDK runtime dependency lands in wave 2 instead of wave 4
deviations.reason: t9 (wave 2) cannot import the docker SDK unless pyproject declares it, but the plan assigned dependency pinning to t14 in wave 4. Sequencing the plan strictly would force t9 to either edit a file the plan gave to another task or build against an uninstallable import. Landing only the dependency early (docker>=7.1,<8, probed as SDK 7.2.0 against engine 29.1.3 / API 1.52); t14 retains the README rewrite, the zero-dependency claim removal, the explain catalog, and the version bump.
